target_customer: Pharma and biotech partners that license drug candidates for mechanically driven diseases
problem: Many diseases such as asthma and fibrosis involve cell contraction, but drug screens rarely measure cell force; Forcyte used bioMEMS devices to measure it at screening scale.
business_model: Drug discovery pipeline, funded by grants and equity

founders.name: Ivan Pushkarsky
founders.background_notes: YC page: technology from his PhD work, Nature BME publication, won SBIR grants.

founders.name: Dino Di Carlo
previous_startups: Co-founded seven life science, diagnostics, device and pharma startups (per YC page)

technical_complexity.rationale: Patented bioMEMS cell force measurement and screening of 10,000 wells a day needed research grade engineering and biology.

defensibility.rationale: Patented UCLA technology plus a dataset of over 2.4 million cell drug timepoint combinations reported in 2022.

market_need_then: NIH funded the contractility assay work through SBIR grants from 2018, indicating scientific demand; commercial demand evidence was not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Playful tagline: drugs that control how much cells squeeze, with ease

branding.brand_signature: Contractome term for the map of cell contraction

brand_strength.rationale: A distinctive coined term and tagline, but little press about the brand beyond funding releases.

outcome_analysis: Forcyte combined NIH grants, a 2019 convertible raise and a June 2022 round that took total support above 5.7M, but the dataset marks it inactive without any report of a shutdown or acquisition. No post-mortem or later news was found, so the cause is not public.
notes: forcytebio.com returned 503 on fetch. The 5.7M total mixes grants and equity; 2022 round amount not stated. The 2019 1M figure is from an LA Tech Watch roundup citing an SEC filing, an outlet only. Conflict: dataset says Inactive; web profiles list Active, undated. A craft.co listing names Robert Damoiseaux as co-founder but no company source does, so not listed. Competitor lists on aggregators were generic, so empty. Exit type unknown.
